bullets.title: Oil surges toward $90/bbl on Iran/Hormuz tensions, then reverses on peace signals
bullets.body: Brent crude rallied 2.1% to $90/bbl (up $10/week) on Trump's tough Iran demands and Hormuz uncertainty, before reversing sharply intraday after Pakistan's defense minister signaled the US and Iran are 'close to some arrangement' and Qatar confirmed Oman-Iran talks are in advanced stage. Crude briefly turned negative after being up 2%+ — the swing reflects algo sensitivity to diplomatic headlines rather than fundamental resolution.

bullets.title: Rising oil/yields create regime split: growth-driven yields = risk-on, oil-driven = headwind
bullets.body: 22V Research draws a sharp distinction between the two current yield drivers: growth-supported 10yr yields (~4.7% on 6% nominal GDP growth and 27% S&P EPS growth) are not restrictive and favor cyclicals; oil/Hormuz-driven yield spikes above 4.7% are a direct headwind for risk assets. The $90-100/bbl range is manageable; $110+ would threaten the risk-on setup. September collars cited as low-cost hedge.

bullets.title: Wednesday CPI seen below consensus; Piper and HSBC expect dovish catalyst
bullets.body: Piper Sandler economists expect July CPI at +0.09% m/m headline (vs 0.20% consensus) and +0.18% m/m core (vs 0.26%), citing shelter disinflation deep into 2027, net tariffs down 50% YoY, and a 70bps CPI/PCE wedge from tech-related inflation. HSBC separately calls it a potential dovish catalyst that could push Fed hike odds further out. JPM's Feroli models headline +0.12% and core +0.22% m/m; NY Fed inflation expectations edged down in July.

bullets.title: Fed on hold into 2027; September hike odds at 44% but oil could change calculus
bullets.body: Piper's base case is Fed holds through 2027 unless core PCE averages 0.3%+ for July-August. A September hike only applies in that tail scenario. Separately, oil-driven yield rises are pushing markets to price higher September hike odds (44%), while SPX vol is pricing only a 56bps breakeven for the Friday CPI/PPI straddle — vol appears cheap heading into the print.

bullets.title: NFIB Small Business Optimism surges to 99.8 in July, highest since Aug 2023
bullets.body: The July NFIB index rose to 99.8 vs. 97.5 estimate and 97.4 prior — the highest reading since August 2023. However, labor quality surged to the single most important problem for small businesses, jumping 8pp from June and 15pp above the historical average of 12%, pointing to a structural skills mismatch rather than demand weakness.

bullets.title: Labor force participation hits 61.4%, lowest since 2021; stock market wealth fueling early retirements
bullets.body: Labor force participation fell to 61.4% in July (lowest since early 2021), with 55+ cohort dropping from 40%+ pre-pandemic to 36.9%. BofA economists attribute the decline primarily to rising wealth from the stock market boom encouraging Baby Boomers and Gen X to exit early — a structural labor supply headwind that reinforces labor quality concerns in the NFIB data.

bullets.title: Yield curve steepens to +47bps (10s2s); term premium rising structurally
bullets.body: The 10s-2s spread widened to new quarterly highs of +47bps. 22V notes term premium is rising structurally driven by federal debt supply and a shift in stock-bond correlation from inverse to positive — a regime change with implications for duration hedging and cross-asset positioning. Reuters poll consensus sees 10yr at 4.34% and 2yr at 3.80% in 12 months.

bullets.title: S&P 500 EPS tracking 32% growth in Q2, but BofA warns deceleration to mid-teens by 2027
bullets.body: S&P 500 EPS is tracking 32% growth in Q2 following 30% in Q1 — back-to-back 30%+ quarters are historically rare. BofA expects growth to slow below 20% by Q1 2027 and to mid-teens for full-year 2027, setting up a tougher comparisons regime and potential valuation pressure at current multiples.

bullets.title: Premarket tape: semis lead, NVDA +1.8%; high-beta momentum in crash mode
bullets.body: NVDA +1.8%, MU +1.6%, WDC +1.6%, SMCI +1.8% pre-market on the $500B AI compute financing announcement. But the tape was bifurcated: High Beta Momentum portfolios were down 3.7% on the session, retail AI chasers lost 1.0%, and SPY barely moved (-0.1%). HIMS -6.9% and CART -3.5% were notable laggards. APP hit a 52-week low, down 5.3%.

bullets.title: Large-cap ETF inflows led the week; consumer cyclical ETFs saw heaviest outflows
bullets.body: For the week ended 8/7/26, U.S. large-cap ETFs topped inflows while consumer cyclical ETFs experienced the largest outflows — consistent with the broader rotation away from high-beta growth into quality and defensives visible in the momentum underperformance this session.

bullets.title: France 30yr yield hits 4.80% — highest since Oct 2008; European fiscal stress rising
bullets.body: France's 30-year bond yield rose 3bps to 4.8004%, the highest level since October 2008, alongside European power prices jumping 20%+ as the heatwave curtailed French nuclear output and Rhine low-water levels halted river cargo. Romania's last nuclear plant faces potential shutdown Thursday — European energy stress is broadening into a macro risk.

bullets.title: NVDA $500B AI compute financing platform: Wall Street reads it as structurally positive
bullets.body: NVIDIA confirmed a partnership with Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to mobilize $500B+ in third-party AI infrastructure capital. Morgan Stanley's Joe Moore sees 10%+ FY29 EPS upside from a revenue-share annuity at 100% gross margin, with third-party funding resolving the 'circularity' concern and reducing balance sheet risk. Wells Fargo reiterates OW with $315 PT; MS reiterates OW at $288.

bullets.title: Memory supply/demand shortage expected to worsen through 2028; HBM pricing up 42% YoY
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Jay Kwon raised FY26-28E memory TAM by 4-8%, projecting DRAM supply/demand shortages worsening through 2028. HBM pricing revised up 42% YoY for next year, supported by longer 8Hi product cycles and slower 12Hi ramp. Agentic CPU demand is underestimated by the market. ABF substrate shortages flagged as the second major semiconductor bottleneck after memory.

bullets.title: TSMC CoWoS capacity doubling annually for 3 years; 98%+ yields on 5.5x reticle
bullets.body: TSMC VP Jun He confirmed CoWoS capacity has doubled each of the last three years and the company now operates 10 advanced packaging plants. 5.5x reticle CoWoS is in mass production with over 98% yields on multiple AI client products. TSMC says it is 'very close' but not yet meeting full CoWoS demand — a supply bottleneck that remains relevant for AI compute buildout timelines.

bullets.title: INTC raises $20B in upsized secondary at $95/share (6.5% discount)
bullets.body: Intel priced a 210.5M share secondary offering at $95, a 6.5% discount to prior close, raising $20B — a third more than the $15B target. The offering is the largest capital raise in the semiconductor space in years and signals Intel's aggressive push to fund its foundry and process node investments. Wolfe Research noted the deal will be discussed on their Aug 14 chip webcast.

bullets.title: NVDA Rubin Ultra tiered HBM specs may increase chip shipment volumes for suppliers
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes NVDA's Rubin Ultra is likely to feature tiered HBM (HBM4e 8Hi high-end, HBM4 12Hi/8Hi lower-end) to address capacity shortages and optimize workloads. Reducing memory content per chip could increase overall chip shipments, boosting volume-driven suppliers. NVDA de-specing was previously cited as pricing noise — this reframes it as a volume opportunity.

bullets.title: Existing home sales fell 1.7% m/m in July; market remains rangebound
bullets.body: July existing home sales declined 1.7% m/m to 4.06M, with all weakness in single-family (-1.9%); multifamily was flat. Inventories fell 1.5% m/m. Morgan Stanley and PSC Macro both flag the print as consistent with a rangebound housing market; 2026 YTD average of 4.08M matches 2025. Morgan Stanley's 3Q residential investment tracking initiated at 0.7% q/q annualized.

bullets.title: Global food prices hit highest since Jan 2023 on heatwaves and geopolitical supply shocks
bullets.body: The FAO Food Price Index rose in July to its highest since January 2023, driven by summer heatwaves and wars in Iran and Ukraine. Cereals, vegetable oils, and sugar rose; declines in meat and dairy were insufficient to offset. US strategic petroleum reserves are simultaneously at 40-year lows, adding to the commodity supply stress backdrop.

bullets.title: Consumer credit rebounds $14.2B in June after May's unusual $1.1B decline
bullets.body: June consumer credit rose $14.2B: revolving (credit cards) +$6.7B, non-revolving (auto/student) +$7.4B. Separately, nearly 1 in 10 US adults are now using BNPL for groceries — a stress signal at the lower end of the income spectrum that contrasts with improving NY Fed job-finding probability (46.2% in July, strongest for households under $50K).

bullets.title: Red Sea / Gulf of Oman shipping attacks escalate; Hormuz disruption risk live
bullets.body: UKMTO reported multiple incidents: a cargo vessel hit by a projectile near Yemen resulting in casualties, a second vessel struck off Al Mokha, and a tanker incident in the Gulf of Oman. Libya's Zawiya Refinery also halted after a drone strike. With US-Iran negotiations fluid and Hormuz transit risk elevated, shipping and energy supply chain disruption remains a live tail risk for the session.
